Let me re-examine `fxGetNextTokenJSXChild`: The buffer starts at `parser->buffer`. Each character in the child text is written via `fxUTF8Buffer`. After 65535 single-byte characters, `p = q = buffer + 65535`. The next character `&` triggers `fxGetNextEntity`. Actually wait, I need to reconsider. The `fxUTF8Buffer` check is `string + mxStringByteLength(character) > limit`. For a single-byte char, `mxStringByteLength = 1`. So the check is `string + 1 > limit`, i.e., `string >= limit`. So when `string == limit == q`, it reports memory error and longjmps. So we can write at most up to `q - 1` via `fxUTF8Buffer`, making `p = q` after writing `bufferSize - 1 = 65535` characters. So after 65535 'a' characters, `p = q`. Then `&` triggers `fxGetNextEntity`: - `*p++ = '&'` writes at `q` (valid), `p = q+1` - `#`: `*p++ = '#'` writes at `q+1` (OOB), `p = q+2` - `x`: `*p++ = 'x'` writes at `q+2` (OOB), `p = q+3` So the first OOB write is at `q+1`, which is 1 byte past the 65536-byte buffer. Looking at the code: ```c parser->rawLength2 = mxPtrDiff(p - parser->buffer); parser->raw2 = fxNewParserString(parser, parser->buffer, parser->rawLength2); if (parser->crlf2) { // ... post-processing that rewrites the buffer } ``` The post-processing only happens if `parser->crlf2` is set (i.e., there was a newline in the text). If I use only 'a' characters and no newlines, `crlf2` stays 0, so no post-processing. Good. But wait, there's another issue.
